rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template: both are short presidential letters transmitting attached draft legislation to Congress to authorize an otherwise unavailable appointment of a named senior general, followed by a concise justification based on the general's exceptional qualifications or accomplishments and a request for prompt congressional action. C03 and C18 share related appointment-specific legislative machinery, but their letters contain substantially more administrative or legal detail and are less close in form and wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I recommend the enactment of legislation which would permit the posthumous appointment of the late Lieutenant General Walton H. Walker to the grade of General
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Attached is a draft of legislation which would permit General George C. Marshall to serve as Secretary of Defense.
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the requested special legislation as permitting a named general to receive or occupy a position otherwise unavailable.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I believe that General Walker's outstanding accomplishments ... fully entitle him to this recognition.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: in view of ... General Marshall's unusual qualifications, I believe that the national interest will be served best by making an exception
shared_material.explanation: Each immediately justifies the individualized legislative exception by emphasizing the named general's exceptional merit.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Attached is a draft of a joint resolution which would authorize this appointment. I hope that it may receive prompt consideration by the Congress.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Attached is a draft of legislation ... I request that you lay this matter before your Committee with a view to obtaining early and favorable action by the Congress.
shared_material.explanation: The closing machinery and sequence closely match: transmit draft legislation, identify its appointment-enabling purpose, and request expedited congressional action.
